identity.title: QoQ-Med: Building Multimodal Clinical Foundation Models with Domain-Aware GRPO Training

problem.claim: Clinical decision-making requires reasoning across heterogeneous data modalities.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal language models are described as vision-centric and as failing to generalize across clinical specialties.

contributions.claim: QoQ-Med-7B/32B, presented as an open generalist clinical foundation model jointly reasoning over medical images, time-series signals, and text reports.
Domain-aware Relative Policy Optimization (DRPO), which hierarchically scales normalized rewards by domain rarity and modality difficulty.
Release of full model weights, a modular training pipeline, and intermediate reasoning traces.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe QoQ-Med as the first open generalist clinical foundation model covering the three listed modalities, and DRPO as a novel reinforcement-learning objective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, after training on 2.61 million instruction-tuning pairs across 9 clinical domains, DRPO improved average macro-F1 by 43% across visual domains versus other critic-free methods such as GRPO.

The authors report that, with intensive segmentation training, QoQ-Med highlighted diagnosis-related salient regions with 10× higher IoU than open models and reached the performance of OpenAI o4-mini.

narrative_sequence.summary: Clinical reasoning spans heterogeneous data, while existing MLLMs are characterized as vision-centric and weak across specialties.
The paper introduces QoQ-Med-7B/32B for joint reasoning over images, time-series signals, and text reports.
DRPO addresses imbalance by scaling normalized rewards according to domain rarity and modality difficulty.
Across nine domains and visual tasks, the authors report macro-F1 gains over critic-free baselines and strong segmentation-region localization.
The authors report releasing weights, training infrastructure, and reasoning traces for reproducibility and downstream research.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a stated data-distribution problem to a reward-scaling mechanism based on domain rarity and modality difficulty.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim is more interpretable when its optimization design explicitly targets the diagnosed source of imbalance.
lessons.application: When proposing multimodal training, map each major data or modality imbalance to a corresponding objective component and state the intended mechanism.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the imbalance is not measured or when a single objective cannot represent the task’s clinically relevant priorities.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs aggregate macro-F1 results with a modality-specific segmentation result and names the comparison baselines or reference model.

lessons.interpretation: Using complementary metrics and explicit comparison targets can make broad performance claims more concrete.
lessons.application: Report an aggregate metric together with a task-specific metric, dataset scope, and named comparison systems when summarizing multimodal results.
lessons.exception: Multiple metrics may mislead when their datasets, evaluation protocols, or task definitions are not directly comparable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the visual domains, baseline implementations, statistical variability, or whether the reported 43% is relative or absolute macro-F1 improvement.
The segmentation data, evaluation protocol, open-model identities, and precise scope of the comparison with OpenAI o4-mini are unspecified.
The claims of being first and novel are author statements and are not independently verified here.
